Subject: Decision-gate control sheets for evaluation and close

Hi Carlos / Elaine —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a first-pass "control sheet" I put together that operationalizes the MAP: it turns the high-level success criteria into concrete acceptance tests, owners, and a recommended close timeline. Key points up front:

- Pilot duration: 6 weeks (2-week smoke + 4-week workload run).
- Exit gates (must be satisfied to move to Reserved/Dedicated): security evidence, performance acceptance, and integration signoffs.
- Core acceptance KPIs we propose measuring during the pilot: p95 generation latency (512 tokens), response concordance (weighted on intent extraction), end-to-end throughput at 80% util, and downstream false-positive rate on critical prompts.

What I attached:
- MAP_ControlSheet_v1.xlsx — acceptance tests, owners, measurement windows, and pass/fail thresholds.
- SLA-draft.docx — draft contract language for the Reserved capacity uplift if pilot passes.

Asks:
1) Can you confirm procurement timelines (target sign-off date for contract if pilot passes)?
2) Please review the latency/accuracy thresholds and flag any showstoppers — my suggestion is to use the thresholds in the sheet as negotiation starting points.
3) Confirm who on your side will own the test evidence (logs, traced requests, labeled samples).

If you prefer, we can run a short working session next Tuesday to walk through the control sheet line-by-line.

Thanks — I want to make sure the MAP is concrete enough that all stakeholders know the decision criteria at each gate.

Best,

Naomi — thanks for the sheet. Quick thoughts from our infra and product teams:

- Latency: 150ms p95 at 512 tokens is optimistic for our current on-prem replicates. Can we relax to 200ms p95 for the first run and re-evaluate on the second?
- Concordance: we like the weighted scoring idea. We need the test harness to include our 120 labeled prompts (will share).
- Evidence: procurement will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and the request log export for the pilot window. Is that available?

We can sign off on the MAP if Redwood can:
1) Commit to two smoke runs (week 1 and week 3) with test artifacts uploaded to the shared drive.
2) Provide SOC2 evidence and a sample request-log export template prior to the first smoke run.

If that sounds reasonable, we should plan the working session Naomi suggested. I copied Elaine — she'll coordinate getting the labeled prompts and timeline.

Carlos / Naomi —

Appreciate the callouts, Carlos. A few proposals to keep the MAP tight while being realistic operationally:

1) Latency compromise: set pilot acceptance at 175ms p95 (512 tokens) for the inference step measured server-side (not including client render). We'll capture client-side metrics separately as an advisory metric.

2) Test plan additions (I attached a lightweight runbook):
   - Smoke run checklist (week 1): connectivity, auth, basic throughput (10k tokens), end-to-end trace capture.
   - Workload run (weeks 3-6): 95th percentile latency, concordance on 120 labeled prompts, and a monthly-simulated spike (x3 baseline) to validate autoscaling/fallback.
   - Concordance pass condition: aggregate weighted score >= 86%.

3) Evidence ownership and uploads:
   - Redwood will upload anonymized request logs and traces to the shared drive after each run.
   - Sage Health provides labeled prompts and the acceptance labeler (or we can run a blinded evaluation).

4) Owners & timers:
   - Redwood test owner: Ben Carter — responsible for smoke run execution and evidence upload (48h after each run).
   - Customer test owner: Carlos / Elaine — provide labeled prompts and procurement sign-off date.

If everyone agrees, Naomi — can you set the working session for Tuesday 2026-11-09 10:00 PT and include the test-runbook.md (I attached a draft)? I can walk the Sage team through the smoke checklist.

Ben
